limitations: Profiled spans are not ordinary request throughput or latency.
Central summary omits the first two and final cycle, and any pair that skips a native CPU generation annotation; all cycles and coverage gaps are retained.

Target graphs require 84 expert GEMMs. Drafter labels require four grouped convolutions per layer: legacy 5/6 rotary calls, or native 5/6 unified attention calls with one extra rotary call and a selector walk. No expert GEMMs allowed.
Other graph types are retained as unknown; a single graph is not a whole cycle.
Kernel unions avoid overlap; group medians need not sum to the median span.
No-traced-kernel time is not proof of a CPU bottleneck: waits/copies/untraced work and profiler overhead can contribute.
Head attribution uses observed production kernel names or CPU GEMM shapes; unmatched head work may remain in other_compute.
GPU annotation fragments with a unique shared CPU invocation name are enveloped to locate graphs. This is not an estimate of active GPU time.
A contiguous captured prefix can be summarized even when later native generation annotations have no captured target graph. Coverage is explicit.
Different outputs, routing, draft widths and runtime policies remain confounders.
